faqs.a: The snake starts in the middle moving right. Press Start, then steer with the arrow keys (or W, A, S, D). On a phone, tap the on-screen arrow buttons. The spacebar pauses and resumes the game.
faqs.q: How do I control the snake?

faqs.a: Eat the red food dot. Each one is worth 10 points and makes your snake one segment longer. There is no time limit — your only enemies are the walls and your own tail.

Two ways: hitting any of the four walls, or running into any segment of your own body. One useful trick the code uses: the snake cannot reverse directly (right into left), which is what kills most beginners.

Slow moves the snake every 180 milliseconds, Normal every 130, and Fast every 90. Food is always worth 10 points, so faster games simply give you more chances to score — and more chances to crash. Start on Normal.
faqs.q: What is the difference between the speed settings?

faqs.a: Yes. When the snake eats, the new head is added but the tail is not removed, so the body grows by exactly one segment. That is why a long snake is harder to steer — every meal adds one more segment to avoid.

snake-game.formula:
Score = 10 x foods eaten.
Each tick: the head moves one cell in the current direction. The tail follows — unless food is eaten, in which case the tail stays and the snake grows by one segment.
Game over when the head leaves the 20x20 grid or touches any body segment.

Three speed settings change how fast the snake moves: Slow (180 ms per step), Normal (130 ms), Fast (90 ms).
You cannot reverse direction instantly — pressing the opposite arrow is ignored, which prevents instant self-crashes.

snake-game.workedExample:
Start: length 3, score 0, moving right.
1. After 4 ticks the head reaches the food. Score becomes 10, and the tail is kept, so length becomes 4.
2. Six ticks later the head eats a second food. Score becomes 20, length becomes 5.
3. The head then turns up into its own body — collision detected, game over with a final score of 20.
